newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Commission on Elections voices suspicion that politicians may have padded the voters' list in the last two days of general registration to cheat in next year's elections. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Majority floor leader Rodolfo Albano says the proposal to convene Congress into a constituent assembly to change the Constitution will be discussed when the Congress resumes its session late next month. (MANILA CHRONICLE)

- The People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action takes a third crack at lifting the term limits on elected officials as it asks the Commission on Elections to authenticate the signatures it has gathered. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The coalition forged by House Speaker Jose de Venecia to strengthen the administration party's hold on the Lower House is bound to disintegrate after the Speaker refuses to yield on his position against the Charter change. (MANILA TIMES)

- Victorias Milling Co and its 31 creditor banks fail to agree on a viable rehabilitation programme for the ailing sugar refiner, prompting some banks to threaten for a foreclosure proceeding (ALL PAPERS)
- Total investment inflows in the country in the first five months of the year surge to 271.12 billion pesos, 18 percent over its target of 230 billion. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co expects to generate additional revenues of about seven billion pesos by end of the year from 28.6 billion if it gets the approval of the national Telecommunications Commission for its proposed rate restructuring plan. (MANILA BULLETIN)
